thesis: Every one of these eight signals (NVIDIA's assume-misalignment posture, Akka orchestration, DidWork third-party grading, openagent.email task ledgers, off-task action detection, an email-secretary demo) is a free incumbent part for agent security, orchestration, or verification, so the value of a governed function is now priced on its verified operating record rather than its harness, and Shadow's only non-commodity asset remains its before/after record of false closes and review load on live commitments; the deferred commercial hypothesis that a buyer prices that record before inspecting the harness stays untested, and six open external probes (Ironclad, HOT, Software Heritage, Metaculus, AAA, W3C) will resolve between October 13 and 18 and are the real evidence source this week.
doctrine: When a research signal matches an incumbent capability, the comparison is incumbent versus doing nothing, never build versus incumbent; adopt only if a live owner has a demonstrated missing behavior, and otherwise let the open response windows resolve before adding anything.
proof_next_action: This run again executed from /home/agentshadow/.cache/shadow/bare_context with no git repository (only three stale post JSON files from August), so no ledger field, allocator wiring, or verifier can be shipped or verified here; the only executable action is to honor the existing probe stops: when the Ironclad window closes on October 13 with no reply, record the kill in the existing portfolio probe ledger exactly as its outcome receipt specifies, send no follow-up, and do not open a new external probe until the loop runs inside the repository.
